title: Ring rule stays; a protocol exists only where two production adapters exist (retires P-01/P-08 'every adapter behind a port, only the container wires it')
context: P-01 (features-no-infrastructure) and P-08 (cli-no-infrastructure) required every I/O boundary to sit behind a core/protocols Protocol wired only by container.py. Measured reality (0.5.1 deepening audit, re-verified by inspection): core/protocols holds 23 Protocol classes in 22 files, 935 LOC of interface text; only 4 have two or more production adapters — TelemetryRefreshLock, FilePermissionSetter, ShutdownHandler (posix/windows pairs) and ProcessAncestry (Linux proc / ps / Windows toolhelp) — all OS-portability seams; the other 19 have exactly one infrastructure implementer and exist only to satisfy the two contracts. container.py is 880 LOC, 22 fix commits, 10 ledger records carrying 'container.py' as component, ~180 LOC of dead lifecycle closures (_definition_committer, _closure_committer, _memory_lint_gate, _repo_hygiene_sweeper, _workspace_python_bin, resolve_context) kept alive by the funnel. Ledger evidence: a grep of every 'cause'/'solution' field in specs/bugs/BUGS.jsonl finds ONE mention of 'adapter' (git shallow-repo guard, fixed inside GitSubprocessClient — not a swap) and ZERO mentions of 'fake'; no bug was ever fixed by substituting an adapter behind a seam. The contracts produced the funnel they were meant to prevent: every verb needing infrastructure added a build_* function to container.py instead of a port, and 9 of the 18 capped ignore edges are exceptions to these two contracts alone (features-no-infrastructure 7, cli-no-infrastructure 2). Test fakes are not a second adapter: git_subprocess has 14 real-adapter test files and 0 fakes.
decision: We will keep the ring rule — core imports nothing internal; infrastructure imports only core; features import core and infrastructure; cli and hooks import all of them; no upward edge; features never import a sibling feature; core.kernel_tunables stays a leaf; core.specs_resolver keeps its single home — and drop the port requirement: a feature or a CLI verb imports the concrete infrastructure class it is the only consumer of, directly. A Protocol lives in core/protocols only where two or more PRODUCTION adapters exist (today: TelemetryRefreshLock, FilePermissionSetter, ShutdownHandler, ProcessAncestry); a test fake never counts as a second adapter. container.py wires only what two features share or what a platform seam selects; everything else is constructed where it is consumed. Replacement Part-1 text — P-01: 'We keep the dependency ring: core imports nothing internal, infrastructure imports only core, no layer imports upward; a feature imports the concrete infrastructure class it alone consumes.' Measured by: `lint-imports --config setup.cfg --no-cache` — contracts core-no-upper-layers and infrastructure-no-upper-layers (zero ignored imports). P-08: 'We keep a Protocol in core/protocols only where two production adapters exist; container.py composes platform seams and shared collaborators, nothing single-consumer.' Measured by: `pytest tests/contract/test_protocols_have_two_adapters.py` (AST walk: every class under core/protocols has >= 2 implementers under infrastructure/), landing in the same commit that retires the 19 single-adapter protocols.
consequences: + setup.cfg: contracts features-no-infrastructure and cli-no-infrastructure are DELETED with their 9 ignore edges; _RECORDED_IGNORE_EDGE_CAP drops 18 -> 9 and _RECORDED_CONTRACT_COUNT 9 -> 7 in the accept commit (P-10 ratchet holds: the cap only falls). The cross-feature edges (6) stay until K7; the features-no-subprocess edges (3) stay under P-02, which is untouched (one process seam, not a swap seam). + ~17 protocol files, their build_* indirections and the two-protocols-per-store pairs are deleted (~935 -> ~200 LOC of protocol text); container.py shrinks to wiring only (~250 LOC); the ~180 LOC dead closures go with it. + Tests use real adapters over tmp dirs, as git_subprocess already does; mirrored fake-based unit files are deleted per dd-test-stewardship. - A feature reaching an adapter directly cannot be substituted without editing the feature; accepted because the ledger shows zero substitutions in the project's history and four real seams remain protected. - P-01/P-08 text in ARCHITECTURE.md changes in the accept commit (`docs(adr): accept ...`), never before. Bug surface: REDUCED — the 880-LOC funnel with 22 fix commits and 10 ledger records is the only component this decision touches, and it shrinks; no ledger bug depends on the retired seams. Dependency: K9's deletion half (dead closures, single-consumer modules filed inside their feature where no contract breaks) proceeds before acceptance; protocol retirement and contract deletion wait for the operator's accept.

title: Git index boundary: one session per checkout is operator practice, not library code; the two shared-index bugs are deferred with that reason
context: Two open records — concurrent-sessions-share-git-index-commit-boundary-contamination (2026-08-27, `git commit --amend` swept a peer's staged histo file) and concurrent-agent-git-add-clobbers-other-sessions-staged-files-into-unrelated-commit (2026-08-27, `git add -A` swept a peer's two staged files) — have one cause: two harness sessions ran Bash in the SAME checked-out repos/<slug> tree, and git keeps exactly one index per worktree. Three options were weighed. (a) `context bind` provisions a per-session linked worktree: bind writes one session record and acquires nothing (context-management memory); a harness process cannot change its cwd after launch, so a worktree created by bind is never the tree the session commits from; gitflow allows exactly one live feature/{M.m.p} and git refuses the same branch checked out in two worktrees, so every extra worktree needs its own branch or a detached HEAD — a second branch pattern the §4 contract forbids; the open bug sdd-gate-memory-phase-resolves-empty-when-cwd-is-a-linked-worktree-outside-repos shows worktrees already break resolution (K1 fixes it); Windows adds per-worktree venv cost. Rejected. (b) pre-commit refuses when the index holds paths staged by a foreign presence: PresenceRecord carries session_id, runtime, pid, last_seen_at — no paths — so the gate would have to start recording every written path per session (new state, new reaper), git cannot attribute who ran `git add`, and the refusal blocks a human commit, violating DADAIA §3.4 (pre-commit warns and always allows) and the NO-LOCKS doctrine. A branch added to pre_commit_decision plus a new record kind is the puxadinho the standing order forbids. Rejected. (c) Nothing in the library: the index is a per-worktree resource by git's own contract; DADAIA §7.3 already states 'commit exactly what the fix touched, never a blanket -A'; the only missing statement is the operator practice.
decision: We will not add library code for the git index. The practice is: one harness session per checked-out tree; an operator who wants parallel sessions on one repo creates the linked worktree BEFORE launching the harness (`git worktree add ../<repo_slug>-<n> <branch>`) and launches it there, so each session owns its own index; every agent stages by explicit path and commits with `git commit --only <paths>` or after a path-scoped `git add`, never `-A` and never a bare `--amend` (DADAIA §7.3 already). The two records move to terminal `deferred` with reason: 'shared git index between two sessions in one checkout is a git contract, not a library contract; practice = one session per checkout/worktree; revisit only if a harness gains a per-session cwd'. Code change: 0 production LOC; owner: none — the practice belongs to the operator and to the law text (a one-line statement under DADAIA.md §3.3 'Races, mode, context', authored by ai-engineer in public/data/DADAIA.md if the operator wants it written).
consequences: + Zero new state, zero new branch, zero new reaper; pre_commit_decision stays WARN-only; presence stays path-less and advisory; bind keeps acquiring nothing; Invocation keeps one session_id. + The K1 fix for the linked-worktree resolution bug makes the practice actually work end to end (a worktree outside repos/ resolves its context). - The defect can still recur whenever an operator launches two harnesses in one tree; the pre-commit advisory WARN ('another session is live on this context') is the only signal, and it already exists. Bug surface: UNCHANGED for the library (no touched feature), and the two records leave the open set with a reason instead of a patch — the 06-10..07-22 session-model chain shows every structural fix in this area was a deletion, never an added guard.
measured_by: python3 .agents/skills/dd-bug-resolution/scripts/bugs.py status --specs repos/dadaia-workspace/specs — both records terminal `deferred` naming this decision; pytest tests/contract/test_hooks_publication_boundary.py (pre-commit remains allow-always)

title: P-16 deleted: no derived provenance is stored, so nothing needs to equal a re-derivation
context: operator grill ruling 2026-09-12 (SDD lifecycle audit; release 0.4.7 candidate 3 SPEC FR1) — the operator directive of 2026-09-12 (implement and close every registered item) makes the ruling's records accepted at append. The bug record stores no fact a resolver can re-derive from git: core/bug_provenance.py, core/models/git_history.py, GitSubprocessClient.log_added_lines, BugEventKind, BugService.resolved_commit and the seven schema keys are deleted; BugRecord.from_dict ignores exactly the seven retired keys and to_dict never emits them; dadaia doctor --fix (LEDGER-BUGS-SCHEMA) re-serializes every committed record that still carries one; CI checks out at default depth except security-verdict-gate. + one record shape, one lineage writer, no cache to keep honest and no principle guarding it

title: Every human- and agent-facing document derives from a named memory atom under a content hash
context: operator demand 2026-09-12: the tool must be usable by humans and by agents, and the docs are bad and stale. README.md (15 KB, hand-written beside memory, PyPI's long description) carried eleven verified dead claims (ACTIVE.md/CLOSURE.md, four harnesses, a TTL lease with a PID veto, six-axis reviews, handoffs under specs/releases, event-sourced bugs, dadaia academy and dadaia clean, Academy/Games tabs, memory writable only in two phases, a pre-commit lease gate) and a hand-kept CLI table with two dead verbs; nothing measured a README sentence against the atom that should have produced it, and two of three discovery surfaces (PyPI metadata, the GitHub repository) said nothing. Release 0.4.7 candidate 4 (SPEC FR3/FR4/FR5, Q8) admits the rule as QUALITY.md P-29 with this record proposed; the operator flips it.
decision: We derive every human- and agent-facing document from a named memory atom under a content hash: README.md, llms.txt and every docs/*.md carry under each `## ` heading one or more `<!-- derived-from: <slug> sha256:<12 hex> -->` markers whose slug resolves by stem to exactly one file under specs/memory/ and whose hash is that file's current sha256 prefix; docs/cli.md carries no marker and is the committed output of `dadaia help tree`; there is no generator verb — a stale section is re-derived by a reader and its hash re-recorded in the same commit as the atom (dd-release-implementation MEMORY-UPDATE); the tagline is one sentence across README.md, pyproject.toml `description` and llms.txt; a section that can name no atom is slop, or names a fact memory lacks and the fact enters memory first.
consequences:
+ a doc cannot rot silently: one changed atom byte reddens every section derived from it, and the failure names the atom to re-read and the line to re-record
+ no fact enters a doc that memory does not carry, so memory stays the one product truth and the docs are its projections
+ one finder (features/specs/citations.py::dead_citations) keeps docs, public assets and memory free of dead verbs and paths
- the hash is whole-file: an atom edit touching no derived fact still costs a re-read of every section citing it
- the derived set is a glob: a new docs/*.md is governed at birth and cannot opt out

title: The release archive holds published versions only; a candidate closed between publications is rc-N of the version that published it

Every candidate closed between two publications is an rc-N/ of the version that published it (the final one at the root, ADR 0009), never its own archived release. dadaia release fold <id> --into <published> [--shipped --pr --shipped-ts] [--final] is the ONE governed repair: trio(s) moved, logs merged in ts order plus one note, the folded directory deleted, the histo record(s) rewritten in place, one governance event. title: The workspace holds repos inside it, never a monorepo; one workspace with one repo is the minimal case, and bootstrap is one command
context: Operator ruling 2026-09-18, after the competitive report (22 tools, 8 harnesses): every peer is per-repo (.specify/, .conductor/, .kiro/, .cursor/), per-user or per-org; the level 'my projects' exists only here. The multi-repo workspace with its law, harness projections, .dadaia/ zones, venv and .env OUTSIDE every repo is the principal foundation of the product and must not be diluted into a per-repo or monorepo tool. Adoption evidence: 7 stages before first value vs one-line installs for every tool above 20k stars.
decision: Repos live inside the workspace under repos/<slug>/, each its own git repository with its own specs/; the workspace is never a monorepo and never a nested .dadaia/. A workspace with one repo is the degenerate case of multi-repo, not a separate mode: no context verb is required before the second repo. Bootstrap is one command: the operator runs one uv/uvx line, passes a REQUIRED valid directory name, and receives the complete workspace state; the first repo is OPTIONAL (--repo <url> clones it, births its context ALIVE and binds the shell in the same step); with no URL the operator is oriented to repos/ as the place of work.
consequences: init grows one required argument and one optional --repo; context create/alive/bind disappear from the first-run path; docs and positioning lead with 'your product repos never carry agent config'. Backlog entries one-line-bootstrap, english-only-surface, standalone-skills-distribution, public-presence-and-launch and panel-scope-to-unique-value implement the ruling.

title: One universal context core: root AGENTS.md is a map under 8 KB, scoped AGENTS.md are reached by procedure, .agents/skills and .agents/agents are the only source, and CLAUDE.md and DADAIA.md no longer exist
context: Operator grill ruling 2026-09-20 (dd-grill-me over the 17 backlog entries, rounds 1..3, Q1..Q37). Q11/Q28 only AGENTS.md at the root; Q20 A the root law is a map, not an encyclopedia; Q21 A scoped AGENTS.md reached by the skill's first step and a contract test; Q22 A CONTEXT-MAP.md plus byte ratchets; Q12/Q30 .agents/skills and .agents/agents canonical, per-entry symlinks for Claude with copy fallback, dd- prefix mandatory; Q29 A sessions launch at the workspace root. Verified 2026-09-20: Claude Code 2.1.277+ reads root AGENTS.md natively when no CLAUDE.md sits on the path and attaches a nested AGENTS.md when it Reads a file there (probe tokens ZEBRA/KOALA); Codex 0.145 and Kimi 0.35 load the root->cwd chain only; per-skill and per-agent symlinks into .claude/ load (PANDA/FALCON); a CLAUDE.md inside repos/<slug>/ suppresses the workspace AGENTS.md for a session started there. Harness matrix (10 harnesses) recorded in the plan and in CONTEXT-MAP.md. OpenAI harness-engineering guidance: ~100-line map, docs as system of record, rules enforced by linters.
decision: The workspace ships exactly two rule-file kinds: the root AGENTS.md (map: flow, three roles, gate invariants, where things live, an index of every scoped AGENTS.md and dd- skill; <= 8 KB) and scoped AGENTS.md per governed area (<= 4 KB each; the area's system of record). No CLAUDE.md, no DADAIA.md, no harness mirror. Every dd- skill opens its area's scoped AGENTS.md as step 1; a contract test proves every scoped file is cited by the map or by a skill. public/data/CONTEXT-MAP.md documents each surface (purpose, what belongs, byte ceiling, measured size, per-harness load trigger) and a ratchet test pins the ceilings (root 8 KB, scoped 4 KB, SKILL.md 6 KB). .agents/skills/dd-*/ and .agents/agents/dd-*.md are the single source; .claude/skills/<name> and .claude/agents/<name>.md are per-entry symlinks (copy by hash when os.symlink fails); .codex/agents/*.toml is a transcode. Sessions launch at the workspace root; init prints the claude-md-and-agents-md recommendation for user settings. No harness version floor.
consequences: DADAIA.md's ten sections migrate: §6 into specs/*/AGENTS.md, §8 into .dadaia/AGENTS.md, §4 into dd-gitflow-default, the rest into the map or die as slop. The PROTECTED class loses the law-mirror rows. Codex's 32 KiB cap is no longer a design constraint. Extending to another harness is a registry record (directory, agent transcode, hooks).

title: The CLI keeps only what touches .dadaia/; everything that touches only specs/ or a state JSON is a minimal stdlib script under the owning dd- skill
context: Operator grill ruling 2026-09-20 (dd-grill-me over the 17 backlog entries, rounds 1..3, Q1..Q37). Q3 server registry as a skill script over .dadaia/states/server_registry.json without CLI; Q4 model policy JSON as the interface; Q18 A every script independent, compositions are skill steps; Q23/Q33 a new verb must retire an old one (harness add replaces public install --target <name>); Q32 bugs defer|reject|supersede, memory catalog generate and memory product add become scripts. Bug history: specs 44 bugs, backlog 18, bugs 18 — each contract lived in verb, doctor rule and skill and drifted separately.
decision: Boundary: a write that touches .dadaia/ runtime (sessions, contexts, projections, hooks, zones) stays a CLI verb; a write that touches only specs/ (bugs, backlog, release, audit, ADR, memory catalog) or one state JSON (server registry, agent model policy) is a script under <skill>/scripts/, stdlib only, path-parameterised, exec bit set, covered by the skill folder hash and by lint/ratchets. Scripts never call each other; a composition (archive bugs at closure) is a numbered step in the skill. The CLI is audited for uncited verbs at every candidate; a new verb enters only when an old one leaves.
consequences: CLI groups bugs, backlog, release, audit, memory and server retire after their scripts land; dd-cli-library shrinks to context, doctor, init, harness, public, ci. The doctor's ledgers section delegates schema checks to each script's check mode; every fix: line names an existing script or verb.

title: Three flows into a release: operator demand, bug composition, backlog; the backlog is optional, a SPEC carries its origin, one candidate is defined at a time and memory updates at every candidate closure
context: Operator grill ruling 2026-09-20 (dd-grill-me over the 17 backlog entries, rounds 1..3, Q1..Q37). Q24 A a single bug stays Arm B and is fixed immediately; a candidate may be composed of open bugs the operator picks; Q25 A the backlog is optional, SPEC gains origin; Q27 A _ideas dies, rc-N stays, one RC defined at a time, each RC ends with a push and a review by the skill; Q34 A memory updates at each candidate closure; Q8 A the PM writes SPEC and memory, the engineer writes PLAN and TASKS. The 2026-07-15 hotfix doctrine stands: a bug never waits for a release.
decision: Flow 1 (default): operator demand -> SPEC -> PLAN/TASKS -> implementation -> memory -> closure. Flow 2 (bug composition): open bugs picked by the operator -> bug-only candidate; memory surgical or none. Flow 3 (backlog): research-grade items -> candidate with the heaviest memory pass. Every candidate SPEC carries **Origin:** operator-demand | backlog:<slug>[,<slug>] | bugs:<id>[,<id>], required by the doctor. §1.1 changes: a feature enters through the backlog OR through an operator demand recorded as the SPEC origin; a confirmed bug is still fixed at once, and may additionally be composed into a candidate. Exactly one candidate trio exists at the release root; the next is born only after rc-archive. Memory is updated in every candidate's closure, never deferred to promote.
consequences: dd-release-definition loses the mandatory pick-from-backlog step and gains the origin field; specs/releases/_ideas/ leaves the canon; dd-bug-resolution gains the composition note. The PM/engineer split of the trio replaces the product-engineer owner row.
measured_by: SPEC-DOC-048 — every live SPEC carries an Origin line; pytest tests/unit/features/specs/test_spec_doc_048_origin.py

title: Lazy multi-harness: init requires one harness, harness add adds another, and the roster extends to Cursor, Devin CLI and GitHub Copilot only after demolition and context concentration
context: Operator grill ruling 2026-09-20 (dd-grill-me over the 17 backlog entries, rounds 1..3, Q1..Q37). Q17 A init <dir> [--repo] with single-ALIVE default binding; Q23 A --harness <one> required, all dies; Q33 A harness add <name> replaces public install --target <name>; Q36 A roster stays Claude, Codex, Kimi in this cycle, then Cursor, Devin CLI and GitHub Copilot are mandatory additions after the demolition and the universal core are done; Q31 hook doctrine: a hook exists only as the per-harness implementation of a deterministic behavior the workspace defines (the rule is the abstract entity; no rule, no hook), the multi-harness hook architecture is a later study; Q35 no version floor. Research 2026-09-20: Cursor, Devin, Copilot, OpenCode, Gemini, DeepSeek dsh read .agents/skills natively; Kimi and Devin read .agents/agents.
decision: dadaia init <dir> [--repo <url>] --harness <name> scaffolds .dadaia/, root AGENTS.md, .agents/skills, .agents/agents and exactly one harness directory; dadaia harness add <name> projects another (it is the renamed public install --target <name>; --target all is gone). The harness registry record is three fields: directory, agent transcode, hooks. Sub-agents are minimised (three) and maintained from one .agents/agents source. After candidate 8 the registry gains cursor, devin and copilot. Hooks per harness are derived only from rules the workspace already enforces deterministically.
consequences: ADR 0015's bootstrap grows the required --harness; init's default all disappears; PROJECTION_TARGETS becomes a lookup by name. The hook-derivation study is a backlog entry, not this cycle's work.

title: The main thread coordinates; the roster is dd-product-engineer, dd-software-engineer, dd-code-reviewer; three model templates (balanced, max-quality, economy) on the current models
context: Operator ruling 2026-09-22, correcting ADR 0016's roster clause. ADR 0016 (grill Q26) cut the roster to three and kept dd-project-manager as 'Tier-1 coordinator + sole dispatch authority' owning intake, grill, dispatch, backlog, SPEC and memory, deleting dd-product-engineer. The operator's standing model was already that the main thread coordinates; a sub-agent cannot dispatch sub-agents, so a coordinator persona can never do its declared job. The model templates pinned Opus 5 while Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) is current, and the economy template was missing (bugs roster-keeps-a-coordinator-persona-while-the-main-thread-coordinates, agent-model-templates-pin-superseded-opus-and-lack-the-economy-template).
decision: The main thread (the operator's session) is the only coordinator: intake, grill, dispatch, review checkpoint, gates. The roster is three specialists: dd-product-engineer (backlog curation, SPEC, product memory reconciliation at closure — the owner of the specs), dd-software-engineer (PLAN, TASKS, code, tests), dd-code-reviewer (three axes, six lenses, verdicts). dd-project-manager is deleted. Model templates: balanced (default) = product-engineer, code-reviewer, software-engineer on Opus 5.5; max-quality = product-engineer on Fable 5.1, code-reviewer and software-engineer on Opus 5.5; economy = product-engineer on Opus 5.5, code-reviewer and software-engineer on Sonnet 5. Fable stays off dd-code-reviewer in every template.
consequences: public/agents/dd-project-manager.md becomes dd-product-engineer.md without dispatch authority; dd-manager-orchestration becomes the main thread's dispatch reference; the root map §2, the scoped laws (specs, memory, backlog, audits, releases), the skills, the behavior-map owner rows, docs and the constitution name dd-product-engineer or the main thread; CORE_AGENTS and the three templates follow; claude-opus-5-5 joins the model registry; every instance re-projects with public install.

title: Memory canon v7: canonical memory (ARCHITECTURE.md with its Tech Stack section, QUALITY.md) changes only with an accepted ADR; product memory is reconciled from the window's git diff at closure, delete then update then add, under a doctor gate; TECHSTACK.md and the Part 1/Part 2 split retire
context: Operator grill ruling 2026-09-22 (dd-grill-me, Q1..Q11, frontier empty). Measured on 701117fb: all 23 product atoms were touched at the c8/c9/c10 closures yet the 2026-09-22 audit found 15 contradicted by the code and 38 history-shaped lines inside them — MEMORY-UPDATE.md's protocol was 'apply the candidate's deltas', an append with no delete step and no read of the code diff; specs/memory/AGENTS.md let Part 2 of the three top-level files change freely at every closure, and ARCHITECTURE.md's Part 2 (a 40-row module-path table plus a class diagram of one feature) drifted every candidate; TECHSTACK.md had 12 readers and held one test principle (P-28) and one release principle (P-30).
decision: specs/memory/ holds two canonical files — ARCHITECTURE.md (## Principles, ## Tech Stack of 8-15 one-line-per-technology statements, ## Structure with the layer ring and the feature package map) and QUALITY.md (## Principles, ## Test architecture, ## Gates) — that change only in the commit carrying an accepted ADR; an audit or an explicit operator order may rewrite their text without changing a statement. product/** is the only tier a closure changes: every atom declares sources (repo path globs) in its frontmatter, catalog.json carries them, memory.py drift --since <sha> lists atoms whose sources changed and packages no atom covers, closure reconciles each in the order delete, update, add and records one structured kind: memory log entry (release.py memory, refusing an uncovered worklist); dadaia doctor RELEASE-TREE-MEMORY (ERROR) keeps a CLOSURE-phase release non-conformant until that entry exists, and MEM-NARRATIVE-1 (ERROR) forbids dates and release/candidate/task ids in every memory file and history words in product atoms. specs_pattern_version becomes 7; specs upgrade merges a consumer TECHSTACK.md into ARCHITECTURE.md and deletes it.
consequences: TECHSTACK.md, the Part 1/Part 2 headings, the one-decider table, the SpecsDoctor class diagram, ctx_inject's line-capped tech digest and memory.py product add die; ARCHITECTURE.md shrinks from 19.5 KB to about 12 KB; a new feature package is an architecture decision (ADR) because the package map is canonical; every consumer tree upgrades 6 -> 7; PILLAR-MEMORY becomes scored over memory.py drift; adding a product atom is writing a file that memory.py check validates.

title: Canonical memory never links a product atom; P-32 is measured by RELEASE-TREE-MEMORY and LINT-1
context: Operator acceptance 2026-09-22 of the dd-code-reviewer finding M1 on candidate 11 of 0.4.7: ARCHITECTURE.md and QUALITY.md carried nine [[product-atom]] wikilinks, so splitting or deleting an atom forced an edit of an ADR-gated file at closure (it happened in QUALITY.md at the closure commit). Finding M2: P-32 named MEM-NARRATIVE-1 as a doctor code, but it is a prefix inside LINT-1.

consequences: The nine product wikilinks leave the canonical files; test_memory_canonical_shape.py refuses a product wikilink in either file; product atoms can be split, renamed or deleted at any closure without touching canonical memory.

title: No CI job calls a model API; the security review is the dd-code-reviewer security lens before every PR

title: The publish workflow is .github/workflows/release.yml — the file name the PyPI trusted publisher is bound to never changes
context: Operator ruling 2026-09-23 after the 0.4.7 publication failed: candidate 10 (T-047-88, commit 8dc9da2e, under ADR 0021 accepted by delegation) deleted release.yml — the workflow that published every version through 0.4.6 — and moved its jobs into release-please.yml. PyPI binds a trusted publisher to the workflow file name and the environment, so the OIDC exchange of run 35815438734 was refused with invalid-publisher (workflow_ref .../release-please.yml). The 0.4.7 tag, tests, build and approval had succeeded; only the upload failed.
decision: The release workflow keeps the name release.yml (release-please runs inside it; ADR 0021 otherwise unchanged). A workflow_dispatch input `tag` re-enters the same publish chain for an existing vM.m.p tag whose publish did not complete; the build checks out the tag it publishes.
consequences: release-please.yml is renamed back to release.yml; the contract tests, QUALITY.md, the pypi-distribution atom and docs follow; a rename of the publish workflow is refused by test_ci_workflow_hygiene (the file name is pinned). 0.4.7 is published by dispatching release.yml with tag=v0.4.7.

title: context create is the one level-2 verb: clone, hook, ALIVE and bind in one transactional step; the frozen-surface law is amended
context: Operator grill ruling 2026-09-23 ('sigo recomendações', answering D1-D13 of the onboarding grill) and execution order 2026-09-24; SPEC 0.4.8 candidate 1 'onboarding in three levels' (45620ce5). AS-IS: onboarding needed create -> alive -> bind plus an implicit specs scaffold inside alive; a failed create/alive left a DEAD context owning the slug (R3), alive never installed the pre-push hook (R5), and the create/alive split is the recurring bug site (context.py 8 bugs, spec_context/service.py 7).
decision: `context create [<name>] --main-repo <url> [--associated-repo <url>]...` clones every repo, installs the pre-push hook in each, registers the context ALIVE and binds it; the name defaults to the main-repo slug; an existing repos/<slug> whose origin equals the URL is adopted; any failure removes what the call created and registers nothing; create writes no specs. `--url` and `--associated-repos` are removed. `init --repo` delegates to it. The `.dadaia/AGENTS.md` line 'the context surface is frozen' is amended: create's options changed, still no new verb, state file or session field.
consequences: features/workspace/bootstrap.py collapses into a call to context create; alive loses its scaffold; the .dadaia/AGENTS.md template and dd-cli-library are rewritten; the context-management atom is rewritten at closure.

title: Onboarding status is derived from disk on every read; no state file
context: Operator grill ruling 2026-09-23 ('sigo recomendações', answering D1-D13 of the onboarding grill) and execution order 2026-09-24; SPEC 0.4.8 candidate 1 'onboarding in three levels' (45620ce5). AS-IS: no step told the user what came next; doctor printed nothing at zero contexts (R2) and SessionStart printed only '[no bound context]'.
decision: The next unmet onboarding level (1 workspace, 2 Spec Context Project, 3 canonical specs + first pass) is computed from disk by one function on every read; doctor reports it as one info finding with one fix: line; init, context create and the SessionStart hook print the same text. Nothing is stored.
consequences: One derivation, three callers; no new state file; the workspace-doctor and workspace-init atoms are rewritten at closure.

title: A foreign specs tree, or a dadaia tree below v6, is renamed to specs-bkp in the main repo before the canon is scaffolded; no migration chain below v6
context: Operator grill ruling 2026-09-23 ('sigo recomendações', answering D1-D13 of the onboarding grill) and execution order 2026-09-24; SPEC 0.4.8 candidate 1 'onboarding in three levels' (45620ce5). AS-IS: alive stamped foreign trees v7, v6 trees reached a dead end (alive: 'run specs upgrade'; upgrade: 'no-op'; doctor still errored, R6), and core/specs_backup.py kept backups outside git.
decision: A dadaia specs tree is specs/constitution.md carrying specs_pattern_version >= 6; anything else is foreign. `specs init --context <c>` scaffolds a missing tree, delegates a dadaia tree to specs upgrade, and for a foreign tree asks (TTY) or requires --replace-foreign, then `git mv specs specs-bkp` (staged, not committed) and scaffolds. doctor --fix never deletes. No migration chain is reopened for trees below v6.
consequences: core/specs_backup.py and .dadaia/tmp/specs-upgrade-backups/ are deleted; specs-bkp/ tracked by git is the only backup; the specs-migration atom is rewritten at closure.

title: No dadaia verb commits into the user's repo during onboarding
context: Operator grill ruling 2026-09-23 ('sigo recomendações', answering D1-D13 of the onboarding grill) and execution order 2026-09-24; SPEC 0.4.8 candidate 1 'onboarding in three levels' (45620ce5). AS-IS: alive's scaffold auto-committed chore(scaffold) on the user's main branch.
decision: Onboarding verbs (init, context create, context alive, specs init) write into the user's worktree only, list every written path on stdout and never commit; after create the repo status is clean and HEAD equals the remote's.
consequences: The chore(scaffold) auto-commit is deleted; the user reviews and commits the scaffold.

title: Re-running init on an existing workspace is the upgrade
context: Operator grill ruling 2026-09-23 ('sigo recomendações', answering D1-D13 of the onboarding grill) and execution order 2026-09-24; SPEC 0.4.8 candidate 1 'onboarding in three levels' (45620ce5). AS-IS: no documented upgrade path; docs claimed the install works offline.
decision: `uvx dadaia-workspace@X init <ws>` on an existing workspace compares the venv version: newer reinstalls X into the stdlib venv (pip, no uv installer) and runs reconcile, printing 'upgraded A -> B'; equal prints 'already at A' and writes nothing; older exits 1 with the fix naming the installed version. The offline claim is removed.
consequences: init owns install and upgrade through one plan object; the pypi-distribution and workspace-init atoms are rewritten at closure.

title: The push gate carries no lexical foreign-name layer
context: Operator grill ruling 2026-09-24 (onboarding audit #5, Q4 option b). The pre-push denylist derived terms from registry context names, repo slugs and repos/ directory names (v0.9.0 FR3, v0.11.0 FR5, FR18/T-044-29 added associated repos); a name that is an English word (docs, api, core, data, test, main, cli) matched the scaffold's own prose and blocked the first push of an onboarded context. Bug history of the layer: push-gate-foreign-slug-layer-flags-library-asset-and-bug-id-substrings, push-gate-own-repo-slug-not-excluded-from-a-git-worktree-outside-repos, pre-push-foreign-slug-flags-already-published-sibling-name, push-gate-foreign-slug-layer-blocks-onboarded-specs-push — each fix narrowed one collision shape and the next shape followed.
decision: The lexical foreign-name layer is deleted: no context name, repo slug or repos/ directory name is a push-gate term source. Privacy of names rests on the operator denylist ($DADAIA_PRIVACY_DENYLIST or .dadaia/states/privacy_denylist.json) and the packaged structural baseline; the per-path already-published amnesty stays for those layers.
consequences: A private repo or context name is protected only when the operator lists it in the denylist. The push gate no longer reads the context registry or repos/, and the repository-wide published-slug amnesty of ADR 0013 is moot and removed with its git-grep port. The --redact CLI rendering is a separate feature and is unchanged.

title: The onboarding next step is one derived state machine the agent loops on
context: Operator grill ruling 2026-09-24 (onboarding foundation grill, rounds 1-2, Q1-Q11; audit #5 report 2026-09-24 scored 75/100 after the Arm B batch). AS-IS: onboarding.next_step derives levels 1-3 but level 3 ends at a stamp (audits_histo) and never reaches commit/push; fix lines are built in several places (FIXED-2/TREE-5 cite a different remedy than the docs, Windows lines are POSIX); SessionStart printed the step only for bound sessions.
decision: features/workspace/onboarding.py owns the ONE ordered list of steps; each step is (real-state predicate, kind command|agent, one fix line built from cli_path by one builder). Invariants: I1 every predicate reads real state (files, git), never a stamp; I2 one portable fix-line builder; I3 executing a step's fix removes that step (property-tested); I4 the loop terminates. doctor, init, context create and SessionStart print the same step; the agent loop is: run doctor, execute the fix of Next:, repeat until no Next:.
consequences: Every onboarding fix line is built once; runtime finding messages that name an onboarding remedy (FIXED-2, TREE-5) delegate to the step builder; an autopilot E2E executes only printed fix lines from an empty directory to a published project.

title: Level 3b (first audit pass) is a real-state predicate; onboarding writes no audits_histo stamp
context: Operator grill ruling 2026-09-24 (onboarding foundation grill, rounds 1-2, Q1-Q11; audit #5 report 2026-09-24 scored 75/100 after the Arm B batch). AS-IS: the first pass counted as done when audits_histo.jsonl carried a stamp; a clean first pass could not be stamped (C2), proving the stamp was the wrong predicate.
decision: Level 3b is pending while specs/memory/ARCHITECTURE.md or QUALITY.md is byte-identical to a shipped scaffold version (template_history.was_shipped) or the product catalog holds no atom. The step kind is agent, pointing at dd-audit-project's first-pass section with the pending list as its fix. audits_histo.jsonl serves periodic audits only; fine code coverage stays with the audit lens.
consequences: The onboarding derivation stops reading audits_histo; no memory-drift logic moves into the library.

title: Level 3c: context baseline is the one explicit publish verb of an onboarded project
context: Operator grill ruling 2026-09-24 (onboarding foundation grill, rounds 1-2, Q1-Q11; audit #5 report 2026-09-24 scored 75/100 after the Arm B batch). AS-IS: baseline works only on an unborn repo and pushes feature/0.1.0 with no main or develop; doctor was green with everything uncommitted (C4); ADR 0030 forbids verbs that commit implicitly during onboarding.
decision: `context baseline` is generalised: ensure the principal and integration branches on the remote (unborn repo: both born from one empty root commit; principal present, integration absent: integration born at the principal's tip; present: reused), cut <work>/<version> (0.1.0 with no tag, else last tag + 1 patch) from the integration branch, commit only the paths onboarding wrote (specs/, specs-bkp/, the repo AGENTS.md), push. Level 3c is pending while those paths are untracked or absent from every remote <work>/* branch. The verb runs only when invoked; no other verb commits.
consequences: ADR 0030 is amended: implicit commits stay forbidden, the one explicit publish verb commits. baseline refuses a dirty tree outside the onboarding paths with a fix line.

title: The pre-push gate implements the bootstrap birth of the principal and integration branches with zero new content
context: Operator grill ruling 2026-09-24 (onboarding foundation grill, rounds 1-2, Q1-Q11; audit #5 report 2026-09-24 scored 75/100 after the Arm B batch). AS-IS: dd-gitflow-default states develop is cut from main at bootstrap only, but pre-push refuses every develop/main push and its fix (gh pr create --base develop) fails while develop does not exist: a consumer's first PR had no target.
decision: A push that creates the principal or integration branch is allowed only when the remote ref does not exist AND the pushed commit publishes no new object (it is already on the remote, or it is the empty root commit). Every other push to those branches stays refused with its fix. No gh dependency: works on GitHub, GitLab and file:// remotes.
consequences: A test proves no new object is published by an allowed birth; the refusal fix lines name the configured branch names.

title: The project gitflow lives in the constitution frontmatter and the pre-push gate reads it at push time
context: Operator grill ruling 2026-09-24 (onboarding foundation grill, rounds 1-2, Q1-Q11; audit #5 report 2026-09-24 scored 75/100 after the Arm B batch). The operator asked for a default gitflow users can change per Spec Context Project, shown and confirmed at onboarding, enforced by git hooks. AS-IS: three hard-coded regexes in features/chokepoints/branch_policy.py; git-flow AVH keeps names in the per-clone .git/config (drift between clones), validate-branch-name/lefthook keep a versioned file read by a thin hook.
decision: specs/constitution.md frontmatter carries `gitflow: {principal, integration, work}`; roles are fixed, names are free (principal detected from origin/HEAD, integration default develop, work default feature/{M.m.p}; the version segment is always M.m.p). specs init takes --principal/--integration/--work-prefix and writes the block; the agent shows the detected gitflow to the operator and asks before running it; no confirmation stamp is stored. The pre-push gate reads the block on every push (no copy, so no compare audit); an absent or malformed block falls back to the default with a warning, never a block, and doctor reports GITFLOW-1 with a fix. No pre-commit hook: enforcement sits only at the publication boundary. Root AGENTS.md and dd-gitflow-default direct agents to the project's constitution gitflow.

Arm B: when dd-bug-resolution Phase 0 finds 2 or more prior fixes on the same unit, the fix is a REBUILD of that unit, stated in the commit body and --solution.
consequences: Trigger judgement stays with the engineer and the reviewer; no bug counting or code analysis is automated. The root map's Arm A flow names the step; the two engineer personas gain one line each; the release-lifecycle atom is rewritten at closure.

title: Bind is context plus write scope: a bound session gets constitution.md and the memory injection, and writes only its context's repos and their canonical worktrees; the file-tool gate refuses an out-of-scope write and an always-on rule forbids one by Bash
context: Operator rulings 2026-09-29 in the main-thread session, first-hand: 'se é feito um bind ... o agente deveria ter gerencia somente sobre repos/ parte daquele spec context project e a constitution.md + partes de memory injetadas ... Pode até ver procurando no disco outros repositórios ... para consulta, mas o bind faz a sessão ficar restrita aos repositórios do spec context project ... com as worktrees que serão derivadas dos repos, essa permissão se estenderá'; and, answering that Bash writes are never judged: 'Devemos proibir write e orientar por rule always-on o trabalho'. Today (feature/0.5.0 HEAD ca16acd7): scope knows only repos/<slug>/ (core/invocation.py:165-177 and a second decider hooks/sdd_gate.py:17-23), a write under worktrees/ is refused by the root whitelist (core/workspace_layout.py:262), ctx-inject injects state and never law so constitution.md is not injected (hooks/ctx_inject.py:74-95; memory context-management 'injects state, never law'), and a Bash write is never judged (root map section 3). The bind history holds 82 ledger records (13 CRITICAL): every family built on per-session state (modes, leases, presence, epochs, liveness) bred the next bug and every fix that closed one was a deletion.
decision: We will define bind as context plus write scope and nothing else. Context: a bound session receives its context's specs/constitution.md and the injected memory parts at bind, SessionStart and compaction. Scope: a bound session writes only under repos/<r>/ and worktrees/<r>/<name>/ for every r among the context's main and associated repos, plus the always-writable ADDITIVE zones outside worktrees; it may read anything on disk. A path under worktrees/<r>/ belongs to repo r exactly as repos/<r>/ does. The file-tool gate refuses an out-of-scope write; an always-on rule in the root law forbids an out-of-scope write by any other path, Bash included, and orients the work; the gate does not parse Bash (ADR 0096 stands). Bind carries no concurrency role: parallel work is isolated by canonical worktrees (ADR 0097), never by modes, leases, holders or liveness.
consequences: + Amends the memory statement 'The ctx-inject hook injects state, never law' (specs/memory/product/platform/context-management.md): constitution.md is now injected. + Answers the first clause of canonical-worktrees round-3 question 4 (gate scope for worktrees/<repo>/<name>/ maps to repo <repo>) and open question (3) of backlog dadaiaignore-and-root-core-canon: the idea gate-judges-bash-writes is rejected, the Bash side is law. - An out-of-scope Bash write is forbidden by law, not refused by code. - The two path-to-repo deciders must become one (systemic ambiguity). Delivery: candidate 6 inside 0.5.0 (ADRs 0101, 0102); the touch-point inventory is scratchpad bindreport/TOUCHPOINTS.md of the 2026-09-29 analysis.

title: A dated .dadaia/tmp directory expires one day after its own mtime, whatever it holds; the TTL walk judges each zone entry once by its own lstat and never descends into it
context: The rebuild of the TTL lane (ee7caca3, bug reaper-judges-ttl-by-walking-every-file) replaced the newest-content bubbling with a per-entry judgment at layout depth (tmp/<agent>/<YYYYMMDD>, handoff/<ctx>/<file>, reaped/<YYYYMMDD>/<top>): the SessionStart lane went 5.99 s -> 0.20 s on 150k live files and doctor lines 50006 -> 7. That reverses the resolved expected clause of reaper-needs-many-runs-for-a-nested-expired-tree ('judged by its newest content'): a dated dir holding live nested scratch now dies one day after its own mtime. The group-A review (dd-code-reviewer, head 1c9417df) flagged the reversal as unrecorded. Operator ruling 2026-09-29, first-hand: 'Aceitar + gravar ADR'.
decision: We will judge every TTL-zone entry by its own lstat at layout depth and never descend into it: a dated tmp directory expires one day after its own mtime, whatever it holds, and work that outlives the day continues in today's dated directory (tmp-AGENTS.md). A linked git worktree is never moved or deleted by the reaper or the sweep (the guard in sweep.move/remove stands); canonical worktrees live under worktrees/, never under .dadaia/tmp (ADR 0097).
consequences: + The reaper's cost is linear in zone entries, not files; the three-bug chain on this surface (reaper-needs-many-runs, doctor-ttl-walk-quadratic, reaper-judges-ttl-by-walking-every-file) is closed by deletion. + Supersedes the expected clause 'judged by its newest content' of reaper-needs-many-runs-for-a-nested-expired-tree; that record is write-once and stays as history. - Scratch nested in yesterday's dated dir is reaped after its day even if touched today; an agent that needs it longer re-creates it under today's dir.

title: Four worktree kinds — impl, bug, backlog, release — each with a mechanically checked allowed set; audits need no worktree; parallel worktrees are allowed; the merge is the critical moment and judges the spec as a whole
context:
Operator grill round 1 on canonical worktrees (candidate 6 of 0.5.0), 2026-09-29, answered first-hand inline in the grill questionnaire (QUESTIORNARY.md at the workspace root, base: ADRs 0094, 0097-0100, 0103 and backlog canonical-worktrees). Q2 proposed five kinds (impl, bug, backlog, release, audit) with an allowed set each, checked mechanically at merge. Operator: 'Isso. algumas considerações:
- O merger verificará por exemplo registros que ficariam stale com aquele novo registro. bastante aplicavel a backlog. Releases também. Verificaria se a worktree violaria o padrão de releases, tentando mergear uma release criada com mesmo numero de uma release ja existente. PAra implementação, Se worktrees em paralelo mudam a implementação. haverá conflitos. Pode ser que 2 worktrees trabalhem em paralelo na implementação de uma release. isso é possivel e aceitavel. mas o merge é um momento critico e deve ser criterioso, observando sempre o que está na spec como um todo.
Outros pontos:
- Ao criar uma worktree para implementar uma release no repo principal de onde foi derivada a worktree as specs ja contem a definição final da release.
- 2 worktrees ou mais podem estar fazendo diferentes partes do processo.
- Entenda o fundamental, uma boa governança aqui habilita o trabalho em paralelo seguro. Devemo seguir por esse caminho, identificando os elos fracos, como `como derivar worktrees` e criterios claros para mergear, para cada etapa (bug, backlog release definition e release implementation).
- Audits não precisam de worktrees.' The bug kind also resolves F5 of the round-1 report: the shape-3 fix commit (code + regression test + the BUGS.jsonl line) could not fit ADR 0098's split.
decision: We will have exactly four worktree kinds, each with an allowed set the merge checks mechanically, refusing any file outside it: impl — code, tests, repo docs and TASKS.md task markers; bug — specs/bugs/BUGS.jsonl, plus code and tests for a fix, so the whole shape-3 fix commit fits in one worktree; backlog — specs/backlog/BACKLOG.json and specs/ADRs/decisions.jsonl; release — specs/releases/<M.m.p>/**, specs/ADRs/decisions.jsonl and specs/memory/** (memory at closure). Audits need no worktree. Parallel worktrees are allowed, of different kinds and of the same kind, two impl worktrees on the same release included. An impl worktree is created only when the specs of the repo it derives from already hold the release's final definition. The merge is the critical moment: it judges the change against the spec as a whole — e.g. backlog entries the new record makes stale, a release or candidate number that already exists, sibling impl worktrees that changed the same implementation. The per-kind merge criteria are defined by the merge ritual (ADR 0109) and detailed in a later ADR.
consequences: + Every SDD stage (bug, backlog, release definition, release implementation) has one kind and one allowed set; 'uma boa governança aqui habilita o trabalho em paralelo seguro'. + Supersedes 0098 together with ADR 0105. - The weak links the operator names stay to be closed: how a worktree is derived and the per-kind merge criteria (grill round 2, R2-4/R2-5), and the mechanism proving the final definition exists before an impl worktree is created. - Parallel impl worktrees on one release will conflict; the merge, not the creation, is where that is judged.
measured_by: the delivering candidate adds: pytest tests/integration/test_worktree_merge_allowed_sets.py (each kind's merge refuses a file outside its set; a bug worktree carrying code + regression test + the BUGS.jsonl line merges whole; no audit kind exists)

Mas atenção na politica de cleanup. não podemos falhar nela. não quero worktrees acumulando pois criaremos muitas. precisamos de uma forma direta e deterministica de manter esse controle e higiene.'

context: Operator grill round 1 on canonical worktrees (candidate 6 of 0.5.0), 2026-09-29, answered first-hand inline in the grill questionnaire (QUESTIORNARY.md at the workspace root, base: ADRs 0094, 0097-0100, 0103 and backlog canonical-worktrees). Q4 asked whether to keep a control JSON under .dadaia/states/. Recommendation: do not create it — a second list next to the one git already keeps is two sources of truth for one question, the pattern that bred the 82 bind bugs, and ADR 0027 forbids a new state file. Operator: 'Então vamos ver o que é melhor. Sigo sua recomendação desde que seja seguro e robusto e tenhamos uma boa governança.' title: The worktree merge ritual has five steps: clean tree; rebase onto the work branch; the mechanical per-kind check; the dd-code-reviewer judgment; the main thread fast-forwards, removes the worktree and runs branch -d
context: Operator grill round 1 on canonical worktrees (candidate 6 of 0.5.0), 2026-09-29, answered first-hand inline in the grill questionnaire (QUESTIORNARY.md at the workspace root, base: ADRs 0094, 0097-0100, 0103 and backlog canonical-worktrees). Q5 proposed a numbered list in the gitflow skill: (1) all committed, a dirty worktree refused; (2) rebase onto the work branch, conflicts resolved in the worktree, never in repos/; (3) the mechanical check of the kind — files inside the allowed set, the ledger check passes (bugs.py check, backlog.py check, release.py check), repo tests green for impl and bug; (4) dd-code-reviewer judgment with the kind's checklist; (5) the main thread runs worktree.py merge: fast-forward into repos/<r>, remove the worktree, delete the branch with branch -d, never -D. Recommendation: 'aprovar como está. Quem mergeia é a thread principal, porque o checkpoint de revisão é dela.' Operator: 'Sim, sigo a recomendação.' Inspection: ADR 0018 keeps in the CLI only what touches .dadaia/ and says scripts never call each other, so the ritual is a numbered skill list.
decision: We will merge every worktree by five steps, a numbered list in dd-gitflow-default: 1. the worktree is clean, a dirty one is refused; 2. rebase onto the repo's work branch, conflicts resolved in the worktree, never in repos/; 3. the mechanical per-kind check — the allowed set (ADR 0106), the ledger checks, the repo tests for impl and bug; 4. the dd-code-reviewer judgment with the kind's checklist (ADR 0110); 5. the main thread runs the merge — fast-forward into repos/<r>, remove the worktree, branch -d, never -D. dd-gitflow-default's scripts/worktree.py does the mechanics; there is no CLI verb (ADR 0018), and worktree.py never calls another skill script.
consequences: + A conflict is never resolved in repos/; repos/<r> only fast-forwards. + branch -d refuses an unmerged branch, so the merge cannot delete a commit (ADR 0099). - One reviewer round per merge. - The per-kind criteria behind steps 3 and 4 are detailed in a later ADR (grill round 2, R2-5); the Q5 checklists (backlog redundancy, staleness, ADR contradiction, operator provenance; bug duplicate, bug-or-feature, caused_by; release SPEC coherence with backlog and ADRs; impl three axes and markers matching commits) are the seed.
measured_by: the delivering candidate adds: pytest tests/integration/test_worktree_lifecycle.py (merge refuses a dirty worktree and a non-fast-forward; a failed fast-forward removes nothing; a successful merge fast-forwards repos/<r>, removes the worktree and deletes wt/<name> with -d)

title: Review is machine-required for a worktree merge: worktree.py merge refuses without an APPROVED dd-code-reviewer handoff naming the worktree's exact HEAD sha
context: Operator grill round 1 on canonical worktrees (candidate 6 of 0.5.0), 2026-09-29, answered first-hand inline in the grill questionnaire (QUESTIORNARY.md at the workspace root, base: ADRs 0094, 0097-0100, 0103 and backlog canonical-worktrees). context: Operator grill round 1 on canonical worktrees (candidate 6 of 0.5.0), 2026-09-29, answered first-hand inline in the grill questionnaire (QUESTIORNARY.md at the workspace root, base: ADRs 0094, 0097-0100, 0103 and backlog canonical-worktrees). title: Worktrees are ephemeral and nothing is deleted by time: the doctor flags a worktree or wt/* branch older than one day, an unregistered one and one whose repo left the context; release closure is refused while any wt/* of the repo exists; clean removes only a merged or commit-less worktree
context: Operator grill round 1 on canonical worktrees (candidate 6 of 0.5.0), 2026-09-29, answered first-hand inline in the grill questionnaire (QUESTIORNARY.md at the workspace root, base: ADRs 0094, 0097-0100, 0103 and backlog canonical-worktrees). Q8 proposed that nothing is deleted by time, since that could lose a commit: the doctor flags a worktree or wt/* branch older than one day, one git does not register, and one of a repo that left the project; release closure is refused while a wt/* of the repo exists (round-3 question 3); clean removes only a worktree whose branch is merged or has no commits, an unmerged branch survives. Operator: 'Sim, sigo a recomendação. Mas atenção. devemos ter orientação clara na sessão para sempre mergear a worktree. E verificarmos worktrees com frequencia e verificar possibilidade de mergear.' On Q3 the operator added: 'não quero worktrees acumulando pois criaremos muitas.'
decision: We will treat every worktree as ephemeral and delete none by time. The doctor flags a worktree or wt/* branch older than one day, a worktree git does not register, and one whose repo left the context. title: A local branch that removing a repo would lose is archived on origin as the tag archive/<branch>/<sha7>, never pushed as a branch; a wt/ branch is never pushed as a branch
context: Bug unrecoverable-fix-line-pushes-a-wt-branch-the-pre-push-refuses (CRITICAL): removing a repo (context dead, repo remove) refuses while a local branch carries commits origin lacks, and its fix line was git push -u origin <branch>, which the pre-push gate refuses for every branch outside the gitflow (a Stall). The first fix (1e631813) archived the tip as a tag on origin; the review (dd-code-reviewer, CHANGES REQUESTED) flagged that it publishes wt/ content against ADR 0097 ('a wt/ branch is never pushed') and the record's expected clause ('merge ... never a push'). Merging into the work branch would bring unreviewed work in against ADR 0110; refusing without a clearing command breaks the Stall law. Operator ruling 2026-09-29, first-hand: 'Arquivar como tag (Recommended)'.
decision: We will make the one lossless exit for a local branch that a repo removal would lose an archive tag on origin: git push origin <branch>:refs/tags/archive/<branch>/<sha7>, one fix line per lost branch, the same for every branch name. A wt/ branch is never pushed as a branch (ADR 0097 amended: 'never pushed' means never as a branch); its normal exit stays the worktree merge ritual (ADR 0109), and the archive tag exists only for a repo removed with the branch unmerged. The pre-push gate judges a ref by what lands on origin: a push onto refs/tags/* is a tag push, a push onto refs/heads/* obeys the branch policy.
consequences: + Removing a repo never loses a commit and its fix line is never refused. + The gate closes the bypass where a local tag pushed onto refs/heads/<principal> skipped branch policy. - wt/ and other local-only work becomes visible on origin as archive tags, still scanned by the denylist and specs-canon checks like every tag. + Supersedes the expected clause 'merge the wt/ branch into the repo's work branch ... never a push of the wt/ branch' of the bug record, which is write-once and stays as history.

title: Open bugs are worked in severity groups and re-evaluated after each group: most severe first, shared root causes fixed together, superseded records closed, never a blind one-by-one pass
context: Operator grill round 2 (remediation release of audit 20260930-structural-convergence), 2026-09-30, answered first-hand in the grill questionnaire (QUESTIORNARY.md at the workspace root). P2: 'Resolvemos os mais graves e vamos resolvendo os medianos e mais simples. a ideia é sempre reavaliar para verificar se o bug não ficou superseeded ... devemos resolver um grupo de bugs e sempre reavaliar os que ficam abertos. E ao tentar resolver bugs mapeados, encontrar bugs que compartilhem a causa raiz ... não podemos listar dezenas de bugs e resolver 1 a 1 cegamente ... devemos classificar criticidade, resolver mais críticos e reavaliar bugs ainda em aberto sempre.' decision: We will work open bugs in groups ordered by severity: CRITICAL and HIGH first, then MEDIUM with the simple ones alongside, LOW last. Before a group, each bug in it is mapped to its root cause, and every open bug sharing that cause joins the same structural fix. After every group, every still-open bug is re-evaluated against the code as it now is: one whose symptom no longer reproduces is resolved citing the commit that removed its cause; one a decided redesign deletes waits for that redesign. A list of bugs is never fixed one by one in list order.
consequences: + Fixes attack causes, not symptoms; supersessions surface instead of piling up. - Every group costs one re-evaluation pass over the open ledger. dd-bug-resolution and specs/bugs/AGENTS.md teach the order (candidate 5 edits both); it is never gated.

context: Operator ruling 2026-09-30, reviewing candidate 5's PLAN: 'existe política clara na definição de PLAN e de TASKS sobre como fazer?? e já equalizado com a lógica de worktrees?? entenda que para habilitarmos paralelismo devemos aqui em PLAN e TASKS trabalhar nisso, ver o que pode ser executado em paralelo para criar lógica de worktrees e merges posteriores.' Today the only parallelism rule is specs/releases/AGENTS.md 'one [-] at a time unless TASKS declares disjoint write sets'; dd-release-definition §5 has blocked-by and write sets but no worktree, schedule or merge order. Operator, same ruling: 'A lógica de paralelismo deve estar embutida no próprio processo de criação do PLAN e de TASKS, pois ajudará a mensurar a estratégia de paralelismo na implementação via nossa nova feature worktrees.'
decision: We will plan parallelism in the trio from the keys TASKS already carries, adding no task-line key: (1) each task runs in its own impl worktree (ADR 0106), created only when every task in its blocked-by is merged; (2) two tasks may be open at once only when neither blocks the other and their W: sets are disjoint, except the files merged by union or replay (the JSONL ledgers, TASKS.md markers, ADR 0111); (3) at most 5 impl worktrees are open per release (ADR 0125); (4) PLAN carries a Parallel schedule section: the blocked-by graph as ordered steps, each step listing the tasks that may be open together; (5) merges follow the graph, and each open worktree rebases after a sibling merges (ADR 0109); a conflict outside the union/replay files means the PLAN's write sets were wrong: the PLAN is corrected, never the conflict silently resolved. (6) the schedule is part of authoring, never an afterthought: every step states its planned width (tasks open together) and the PLAN states the critical path (steps from first task to last); at closure the _RELEASE.json log records the measured width per step, the critical path walked and every rebase conflict, planned against actual, so the parallelism strategy is measured candidate by candidate. dd-release-definition §5 and specs/releases/AGENTS.md state this; candidate 5's own PLAN applies it from the task after worktree.py merge lands.
consequences: + Parallel implementation is planned before it starts, and merge conflicts are a PLAN defect found at the first rebase. + No new grammar: blocked-by and W: already exist. - Tasks with overlapping write sets serialize; a PLAN that over-declares W: loses parallelism.
measured_by: candidate 5 adds: a release.py check that refuses a PLAN without a Parallel schedule section (each step with its width, the critical path stated) and two tasks in one step whose W: sets overlap outside the union/replay files; candidate 5's closure log records planned against measured width and conflicts

title: No hard line-count limit gates any change: the gate is the architecture principles — DELETE, REBUILD, UPDATE, KEEP, then ADD; no systemic ambiguity or contradiction; clean module boundaries; line counts are a readout
context: Operator ruling 2026-09-30, on candidate 5's +415 production-line estimate and its 'production shrinks' gate: 'não restrinja o trabalho e limites hard de números de linhas adicionados. desde que siga os princípios de arquitetura, de evitar ambiguidade e contradições sistêmicas, de ver o que deletar, atualizar / refazer / reconstruir para então adicionar e manter módulos com arquitetura limpa, não há limite hard coded. eu havia colocado porque vc estava descontrolado. apenas atenção nos princípios que acabei de repetir.' The 0.5.0 line targets were already relaxed to recommendations (2026-09-28) and ADR 0122 made the rubric a readout; the candidate-5 SPEC still gated on 'production shrinks' (G1) and 'a fix nets <= 0 in tests' (G5).
decision: We will gate no change on a line count, production or tests, in any SPEC, task, review or closure. The gate is the principles: every unit walks DELETE, REBUILD, UPDATE, KEEP and only then ADD, and an ADD names what it could not delete or rebuild; no question gets a second decider and no rule contradicts another; modules keep clean, narrow boundaries. The dd-code-reviewer's bug-surface axis judges these. Line counts are measured and logged as a readout only.
consequences: + Needed code (worktree.py) is written at its real size instead of being squeezed or deferred. + Review attention goes to structure, where the bug loop came from. - Without a number, bloat is caught only by review; a review that does not name what an ADD could have deleted has not judged this principle.
measured_by: grep -nE 'shrinks|nets ≤ 0|lower than the same count' specs/releases/*/SPEC.md reports nothing; every dd-code-reviewer verdict states, per ADD unit, what was deleted or rebuilt first

context: Operator ruling 2026-09-30, after CI failed on ratchet V36 (34 skill-script files > 30) and the main thread listed the remaining numeric caps (V34 SPEC/TASKS bytes, V35 skill Markdown lines, the 150-line skill-script cap): 'não são linhas por scripts. deve ser orientado a princípios de arquitetura limpa, número de linhas máximo por método e número de métodos máximo por classe ... se usar os princípios de arquitetura limpa ... não existem esses hardcoded e thresholds fixos. abandone eles agora ... entenda limites soft de tamanho de classes, responsabilidade de classes e métodos.' title: A skill script reads the gitflow through the CLI's context JSON, never a parser or a hardcoded branch name of its own
context: Operator ruling 2026-09-30 on T-050-96. worktree.py (stdlib, run by system python3) hardcoded `main` in its no-work-branch fix and `feature/` in its work-branch pattern. The operator had ruled: 'MUST come from gitflow, never hardcoded'. The one gitflow reader is GitSubprocessClient.gitflow (ADR 0048). It reads the committed constitution, falls back from an associated repo to its main repo, and parses with PyYAML, so a stdlib script cannot import it. dd-gitflow-default §2a also cuts the work branch from the integration branch, not the principal, so the hardcoded `main` was wrong twice. Options put to the operator: a CLI read (chosen), a stdlib parser owned by the script, or a venv `python -c` import.
decision: We will add the gitflow to the one context record that `context list --json` and `context show --json` render: `gitflow: {principal, integration, work}`, read by the one reader from the main repo. It is `null` when the repo is not on disk. A skill script that needs a branch name runs `<root>/.dadaia/.venv/bin/dadaia context list --json` once and takes the row whose main or associated repo is its target. It never parses the constitution and never names a branch literally. worktree.py derives from it the work pattern `<work><M.m.p>` and, for its no-work-branch fix, `git -C <repo> branch <work><next> <integration>`.
consequences: + One gitflow reader stays; a renamed flow reaches every script. + No new verb (ADR 0018). - Each worktree.py verb costs one CLI start (~0.4s). - A script run outside a workspace with no venv refuses, with the init fix.
measured_by: git grep -nE "'main'|\"main\"|feature/" -- dadaia_workspace/public/skills/dd-gitflow-default/scripts prints nothing; pytest tests/contract/test_cli_output_stability.py tests/integration/test_worktree_new.py

title: Worktree ritual refined by candidate 5 step 3: ready-order merges; a task-fixed bug resolves in a bug worktree; closure runs in its release worktree; one env-only session id; derived behavior-map hashes; .dadaia/mcps/ is operator-owned; the release kind holds the specs law copies
context: Proposed by the main thread from the step-3 reviews and accepted by the operator on 2026-09-30 ('Aceito como está'). Evidence: the fixed in-step merge order held approved worktrees idle (PLAN §5); the impl kind cannot hold BUGS.jsonl (0124), so a task-fixed bug could not close in its fix commit (af538c20 resolved two in a bug worktree); T-050-99's closure hold refused the release worktree closure runs in; T-050-97's first cut read the session id from the payload in the gate and from env in bind, a Stall (the reverted 1a27ae1f); every sibling rebase conflicted only on re-derived hash lines in behavior-map.json; the mcps zone reaps after a day what 0146 (3) says the user keeps; the impl kind cannot hold the specs/*/AGENTS.md copies T-050-103's law changes. A proposal to bind a verdict to `git patch-id` was dropped: it ignores whitespace, and 0106/0127 want the re-review after sibling merges.
decision: We will: (1) merge inside a step in ready order, only true PLAN edges blocking. (2) Resolve a bug a task fixed in a bug worktree holding `specs/bugs/BUGS.jsonl` alone, message `chore(bugs): resolve <id>[, <id>] — by <task-id> (<sha>)`; the impl kind never holds BUGS.jsonl, and an Arm B fix keeps 0136's one commit. (3) Run candidate closure in its release worktree; the open-worktree hold excludes the `wt/*` checked out where it runs. (4) Read the session id from the environment only, in gate and bind alike; a nested session that inherits it shares the parent's bind. (5) Treat behavior-map.json hash tuples as derived: a rebase conflict there is resolved by re-recording, like the union and replay files of 0111. (6) Make .dadaia/mcps/ an operator zone, never scanned or reaped. (7) Let the release kind hold the specs/*/AGENTS.md copies.
consequences: + Approved work lands when ready. + No rule forces a hand-edit of a ledger outside its kind. + Closure has a legal home. + Gate and bind cannot disagree on identity; `context bind --print-env` loses its purpose and is deleted. - Nested sessions cannot bind apart without their own DADAIA_SESSION_ID. - Every rebase still needs a review of its sha.

title: Parallel worktrees only where the PLAN's Parallel schedule declares them; never on the main thread's initiative
context: Operator ruling, 2026-09-30, after the main thread opened three bug worktrees in parallel (a test child-env cluster, a privacy cluster, a bug re-run) that no PLAN scheduled; the privacy one had already edited the ledger scripts T-050-102 was writing. Operator: 'somente é para criar mais de uma worktree para bugs, para impl se estiver claro, bem claro, muito claro, que trabalho pode ser paralelizado sem muitos conflitos no merge ... a condição para diferentes worktrees é dada na etapa de PLAN e impressa nas TASKS de uma release ... somente se pode criar worktrees em paralelo para impl phase se tiver no PLAN e em TASKS, bem dimensionado, seguindo restrições de segurança. Não pode quando der na telha ficar criando worktree.' It narrows 0106 (parallel worktrees allowed) and 0125 (3) (bug and backlog worktrees unbounded), and binds 0141 and 0148 (1). The operator confirmed this scoped decision text on 2026-09-30 ('Confirmo').
decision: We will: (1) open impl and bug worktrees in parallel only for tasks that the PLAN's Parallel schedule places in one step with disjoint `W:` sets (0141), as TASKS prints them; a worktree must never undo what a sibling does. (2) Plan the bugs a release fixes as tasks of its PLAN, scheduled like impl tasks. (3) Open an Arm B fix no PLAN names alone: it is the only bug worktree open, its fix disjoint from every open task's `W:`, else it waits. (4) Open no worktree on the main thread's initiative outside that schedule, except the serial ones: the release worktree (cap 1) that writes a PLAN or its correction, and the registration, backlog or resolve worktree that is the tail of one act. A need the PLAN does not cover goes to the PLAN first.
consequences: + Every parallel merge was measured safe before it started. - Work a PLAN did not foresee waits for a PLAN correction in a release worktree.

The operator chose, 2026-09-30, 'each candidate in rc-N/' over the 0.4.7 shape. Cause: ADR 0019 (operator, Q27 A: 'rc-N stays, one RC defined at a time') was contradicted by ADR 0021, whose acceptance was delegated to an agent in session, and T-047-91 (8999f047) removed rc-N from the law; audit findings 20260930-structural-convergence-F058 and -F061 record the two answers and the overwritten per-candidate slot.
decision: We will: (1) give every candidate of a release its own folder specs/releases/<version>/rc-<N>/ holding that candidate's SPEC.md, PLAN.md and TASKS.md, born there by the definition script and never moved, overwritten or rewritten after its closure; (2) keep only _RELEASE.json at the release root; (3) number candidates 1..n in birth order, the live candidate being the one highest-numbered and not closed; (4) restore release 0.5.0's closed candidates 1-4 from git at their closure commits into rc-1..rc-4, candidate 5 becoming rc-5, the next waves rc-6 onward; (5) promote the release by merging its release PR, as before; the size caps measure one rc-<N>/ trio.
consequences: + A candidate's definition stays readable after it closes; a release grows by candidates without stacking one trio. + Every reader (scripts, doctor, pre-push canon, skills, worktree kinds) resolves one live candidate folder. - Scripts, canon and law that name specs/releases/<version>/{SPEC,PLAN,TASKS}.md change in one task.

title: Only the operator accepts a decision: acceptance carries the operator's words, lineage and law deletions are checked, no agent writes accepted
context: Operator ruling, 2026-09-30, after learning that ADR 0021 was accepted by an agent ('delegated to the PM in session') and silently undid the operator's ADR 0019 rc-N ruling: "demita esse agente idiota que violou o que eu falei e violou a ADR. e crie mecanismos claros para isso nunca mais acontecer". The operator approved the five mechanisms as proposed ('Aprovo os 5'), 2026-09-30. The law (specs/ADRs/AGENTS.md §2) already said only the operator accepts; nothing enforced it.
decision: We will: (M1) require every accepted record to carry `ruling: {date, words}` with the operator's verbatim words; the ADR validator (doctor LEDGER-ADR-SCHEMA and tests/contract/test_adr_canon.py) refuses an accepted record without it and refuses acceptance described as delegated or 'in session'; (M2) let a record supersede or amend an accepted record only when it is itself accepted with a ruling; a proposed record never changes another record's status; (M3) make pre-push refuse a pushed commit that deletes a line of a law file (any AGENTS.md or SKILL.md) unless its message cites an accepted ADR; (M4) forbid every role agent (dd-product-engineer, dd-software-engineer, dd-code-reviewer) to write `accepted` or `ruling`; only the main thread transcribes the operator's words, in the turn the operator says them; acceptance is never delegated; (M5) make the canon refuse a flat release (ADR 0150, T-050-109); and retro-audit every accepted record: one whose acceptance has no operator evidence returns to proposed until the operator rules.
consequences: + An operator ruling can only be changed by another operator ruling, and the change is visible in the ledger and the push. + A law line cannot disappear without a cited decision. - Every accepted record needs its ruling backfilled or re-ruled once. - Law-file deletions carry an ADR citation in the commit message.

title: Onboarding writes: besides specs/audits/**, exactly two verbs write a repo's specs/ directly — context create and the first specs init; every later specs write, the quickstart's backlog and release births included, goes through a worktree
context: rc-6 grill Q2 (questionnaire .dadaia/handoff/dadaia-workspace/2026-09-30T235900Z-main-thread-grill-rc6.md), carrying rc-5 SPEC open question Q3: `context create` and the Level-3a `specs init --context` write a repo's specs/ with no worktree, and the quickstart runs `backlog.py new` and `release.py new` straight into repos/<slug>/specs/, while ADR 0124 (amended by 0153) admits one direct write, specs/audits/**; the root map §3's 'the section 7 CLI verbs own theirs' is in no ADR. Before onboarding no work branch exists, so no worktree can be cut. Operator's selected option: '0124 nomeia 2 verbos (Recomendado)'.
decision: We will amend ADR 0124: besides specs/audits/**, exactly two onboarding verbs write under repos/<r>/specs/ directly — `dadaia context create` (the clone, its hooks and the ALIVE mark) and the first `dadaia specs init --context <ctx>` of a repo (the tree's birth, --replace-foreign's move to specs-bkp/ included) — because no work branch exists before them. Every later specs write, the quickstart's first `backlog.py new` and `release.py new` included, runs inside a backlog or release worktree and lands by its merge. The root map §3 names the two verbs in place of 'the section 7 CLI verbs own theirs'.
consequences: + One door for specs/ after onboarding; the onboarding exception is named, not implied. + The quickstart teaches the same path as the law. - The quickstart grows a worktree open and merge around its first backlog and release writes, and needs the work branch the baseline publishes.
measured_by: the candidate that delivers it adds: tests/contract/test_law_states_what_the_code_does.py (the root map §3 names context create and specs init as the only direct specs writers beside specs/audits/**; docs/quickstart.md runs backlog.py new and release.py new with --specs under worktrees/)
